learn.title: Functions with more than one rule
learn.body: A piecewise function uses different rules on different parts of the domain. Example: use $x+1$ when $x<0$ and use $x^2$ when $x\ge 0$. To evaluate, first decide which part the input belongs to, then use only that rule.

learn.title: Absolute value
learn.body: $|x|$ is the distance from 0, so it is never negative: $|-5|=5$. The graph of $y=|x|$ is a V with its corner at the origin. For $y=|x-h|+k$ the corner (vertex) is at $(h,k)$, using the same shifts as before.

learn.title: Solve $|2x-1|=7$
learn.body: A distance of 7 means the inside is 7 or $-7$.
$|x|=-3$ has no solution, because a distance cannot be negative. Isolate the absolute value first, then split into two cases.

questions.prompt: Use $x+4$ when $x<1$ and $3x$ when $x\ge 1$. What is the value at $x=1$?
questions.explanation: $x=1$ is not less than 1, so use $3x$: $3\cdot 1=3$.

questions.prompt: Same rule: $x+4$ when $x<1$, $3x$ when $x\ge 1$. Find the value at $x=-2$.
Same rule again. Find the value at $x=4$.

questions.explanation: An absolute value is never negative, so it cannot equal $-4$.
$|x+2|$ is $|x-(-2)|$, so the shift is left 2. The $-3$ moves it down 3.

questions.prompt: Solve $|x-1|=6$. Put the steps in order.
steps: Check both in the original equation
questions.explanation: An absolute value equation splits into two cases. Checking guards against slips.
